text:
1. rig-status — the readiness matrix as the percept of rigging
Mirror semantic-status exactly. The seven rows are already machine state; ship them:

Bash
tools/seat rig-status
# { state:"needs_bind", rows:{ connected_body:{status:"blocked", components:2,
#     main:4732, detached:1}, required_semantics:{status:"blocked", missing:
#     ["hand:left","foot:right"], uncoveredBodyFaces:214}, canonical_skeleton:"ready",
#     current_topology_hash:"waiting", ... },
#   weightsStale:false, fitReview:false, bindReview:false }
Two rules carry over from your existing design:

Every refusal names its gate. rig bind while blocked replies with the exact failing rows and their counts — the agent never diagnoses by trial.
Staleness lives in the percept. Your invalidation table (§13) is prose an agent must memorize; instead, any topology/anatomy/binding edit flips weightsStale:true in every subsequent reply. The agent sees the debt the moment it's incurred, same as unnamed.
2. Attach, classify, repair — mostly existing verbs
Bash
tools/seat action rig '{"operation":"attach-humanoid"}'
tools/seat action rig '{"operation":"object-mode","id":"part:hat","mode":"rigid","bone":"head"}'
tools/seat action rig '{"operation":"select-detached"}'   # same contract as select-audit
select-detached is your select-audit pattern verbatim: the host marks faces in the same pass that counts them, selection can't disagree with the number. The repair itself is your existing junction toolkit — delete/bridge/weld-pairs — so the skill doc just points back at the topology finish gate. Note the "root refused for rigid" rule becomes a refusal string, not documentation.

The BODY-must-be-first constraint deserves a pre-attach audit rather than prose: attach-humanoid should reply with which object it's about to make BODY and refuse with a plan when the largest connected mesh isn't first — that trap currently only lives in a warning callout.

3. Anatomy roles — where selection amplifiers pay off
Bash
tools/seat select region:left_arm            # the Names fast path, already yours
tools/seat action rig '{"operation":"role","role":"upper_arm:left"}'
tools/seat action rig '{"operation":"coverage"}'
# → { covered: 4518, uncovered: 214, roles:{...}, uncoveredSelectable:true }
tools/seat action rig '{"operation":"select-uncovered"}'
select-uncovered closes the "16/16 necessary but not sufficient" trap — the fitter's real requirement (complete coverage) becomes a selectable, countable fact instead of a surprise MissingSemanticRoles after the counter reads full.

The boundary-placement guidance ("place boundaries at joint rings, not centroids") should be an audit too:

Bash
tools/seat action rig '{"operation":"boundary-audit"}'
# per adjacent role pair: is the shared boundary a closed ring? its centroid,
# plane normal, width; flag:"ragged" when the transition zigzags across loops
Fit consumes shared boundaries; letting the agent inspect them before fitting prevents the fit-inspect-refit churn. And this is where select-loop / select-between from the amplifier family earn their keep — "the band from the elbow ring to the wrist ring" is exactly the anatomy assignment gesture.

4. Skeleton — absolute placement, per-joint state
Bash
tools/seat action rig '{"operation":"fit"}'
# reply: per-bone {status:"boundary"|"template"|"manual", confidence, origin}
tools/seat action rig '{"operation":"joint","bone":"elbow_left","origin":[x,y,z]}'
tools/seat action rig '{"operation":"joint","bone":"knee_left","lock":true}'
tools/seat action rig '{"operation":"skeleton"}'   # full read: origins, frames, locks, segment lengths
Agents think in coordinates, so joints take absolute origin/frame (the set-position lesson from earlier). Fit's reply must flag every template fallback loudly — that's the "inspect carefully" case, and an agent should treat template joints as unresolved work items, not results. The GUI's Shift-for-1mm precision is irrelevant here; exact numbers are the native lane.

Also: a mirror operation for joints — fit/fix the left side, reflect to right — same amplifier logic as mirror-replace.

5. Bind verification — the part that actually needs new capability
Heatmap and eyeballed bend tests are the two human-only steps. Give agents numeric equivalents plus shots:

Bash
tools/seat action rig '{"operation":"bind"}'
tools/seat action rig '{"operation":"probe","vertex":812}'          # exact 4 influences
tools/seat action rig '{"operation":"weights-summary","bone":"upper_arm:left"}'
# → { vertices: 431, totalWeight, bbox, maxWeightOutsideRole: 0.31,
#     bleedsInto:["chest","lower_arm:left"] }
tools/seat action rig '{"operation":"bend-test","test":"elbow","side":"both"}'
# → per side: { maxDisplacement, volumeDelta: -0.04, selfIntersections: 2,
#     creaseDepth, asymmetry: 0.003 }, plus optional shot paths
Three of these are the whole quality loop:

weights-summary with bleed detection replaces the heatmap: "how much of this bone's influence lands outside its anatomical region" is precisely what a human reads off the colors, as one number.
bend-test with metrics replaces the visual pose check. Volume loss at the elbow, self-intersection count in the armpit, and a left/right asymmetry scalar are things the intersecting-faces audit machinery can already compute against the deformed specimen. Pair each with an offscreen shot of the posed specimen for VLM confirmation, but the numbers are the gate — an agent comparing 0.04 volume loss against a threshold is far more reliable than one judging a crease in a PNG.
weights-symmetry whole-rig: mirrored vertices should carry mirrored weights within tolerance; list offenders. Humans check both sides by habit; agents check what's measurable.
When a bend test fails, the reply should localize it (worstVertices:[...], their roles, nearest joint) so the agent knows whether the fix is an anatomy boundary or a joint origin — the two documented remedies — before rebinding.

6. Durability and the loop
save already exists; extend semantic-status's pattern so rig-status compares saved RJSK vs resident weights (hash match, influence counts) — the cold-reopen proof becomes the same three-horizon discipline agents already know. One process note: rig history is session-resident and clears on cold reopen, so the skill doc must state that undo is not a recovery strategy across reopens for rig work — checkpoint with save instead.

Skill-doc loop, in your established voice:

rig-status before anything; satisfy blocked rows in order (connectivity → coverage → skeleton).
One gate per step; re-read rig-status after each.
Never bind while boundary-audit reports ragged joints — cheap fix now, expensive rebind later.
Bind, then numeric verification is mandatory: weights-summary per limb bone, all five bend tests both sides, weights-symmetry. Shots are corroboration, not proof.
save, cold-reopen, rig-status must read bound with all rows ready without binding again.
Export role last, via the existing model-export role argument.
7. Two structural notes
Kill the F-F dance. "Press F twice to return viewport ownership" is a GUI-focus artifact; the seat should never simulate it. Rig operations should acquire/release the rig viewport internally the way background routing selects and restores sessions — otherwise you'll find agents sending keypress hacks, the rigging equivalent of sleep(4).

Follow applies here too. A human fitting joints and correcting a bad shoulder is a demonstration stream just like Delete Faces → Create Face. Joint-edit events through the rig journal give you the same distill-into-recipe flywheel — fit-shoulder-cluster is a plausible second approved recipe once someone's demonstrated the correction pattern a few times.

If you only build three things: rig-status (the gates as data), select-uncovered + boundary-audit (the two silent Fit failures made visible), and numeric bend-test/weights-summary (the eyes). Everything else in the guide already maps onto verbs and disciplines your agents have.
